hypothesis: The parent's density-weight relaxations all act on the *global* density weight scalar, but the TNS cost comes from *localized* congestion where a few bins stay overfull long after the global overflow has settled; instead of touching the density weight, tighten the wirelength-model gamma schedule so that in the late stage (when overflow is already low) the HPWL model becomes more accurate (smaller gamma), which shortens critical nets without adding congestion — but clamp the gamma floor to avoid the "cells pile up" regime that hurt c014/c018.
expected_effect: TNS improves (more accurate wirelength late => shorter nets, fewer moderate violations), WNS neutral-to-slightly-positive, overflow roughly unchanged (gamma only refines, does not change density pressure), runtime unchanged.
analysis: The hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with no invalid runs. Gains concentrate in TNS (bp-ng45 +24.3%, ariane133 +23.7%) alongside WNS, consistent with a tighter late-stage gamma shortening critical nets without raising overflow (~110–136). bp_fe-ng45 moved least (+7.7% TNS), suggesting the gamma floor may be binding there or congestion already limits it. Next step: sweep the gamma floor per case (especially bp_fe-ng45) to confirm the clamp isn't leaving gains on the table while still avoiding the c014/c018 pile-up regime.
